technique: Self-speculative decode with the checkpoint's MTP head (k chained one-row drafts), one k+1-row verify pass through the target, greedy accept on exact argmax; GatedDeltaNet conv+delta state kept per verify row so rejection restores one saved row state instead of re-running
mechanism: Decode is weight-bandwidth bound; a verify pass reads the weights once for k+1 rows. On Spark a k=2 pass costs ~25 ms vs 11.6 ms per plain step, so it pays above ~2.16 tokens per pass (per-position acceptance above ~0.43-0.46).
impact: localeval quiet slot (fleetq #4399), decode tok/s off -> k=2: 84.3 -> 86.3 at 128 (+2.4%), 83.8 -> 87.8 at 1k (+4.8%), 81.2 -> 88.5 at 4k (+9.0%); acceptance 62.8%, 2.25 tokens/pass. 128 and 1k are within noise (tie), 4k a small win. k=3 loses at 128/1k (75.3 / 80.4). On code/arithmetic prompts (70-93% acceptance) k=2 gave +16-33% in a shared slot. Greedy output token-identical to --spec off (12/12 cases x 256 tokens, k=1..3); verify rows bitwise equal to M=1 decode rows (6,430/6,430).
preconditions: checkpoint ships the MTP head (mtp.* tensors, mtp_num_hidden_layers)
small-M kernels that compute each row like the M=1 launch (CUDA GEMV at q<=3, measured not enforced)
transfer_notes: Output unchanged by construction (accept only on exact argmax of the target's own rows). The win is content-dependent; graph-capturing the verify pass (est. ~+20%) and zero-copy out-of-place GDN state (est. 5-8%) are the next levers. vLLM's MTP is 101.4 tok/s at 1k in the same cell, so this does not close the spec-lane gap.
